# Cūḷasakuludāyi Sutta (MN 79 (PTS MN ii 29))

**ID:** MN 79 (PTS MN ii 29)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Cūḷasakuludāyi Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** The Shorter Discourse With Sakuludāyī

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷasakuludāyi Sutta* (MN 79) records a discussion set at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Sanctuary, while the wanderer Sakuludāyin (or Udāyin) was residing with a large assembly of wanderers at the Peacocks' Sanctuary [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. The dialogue begins with the Buddha asking about Udāyin's meeting with Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta (Mahāvīra), whose claims to total omniscience fell apart when he prevaricated and displayed irritation upon being questioned about past events [Appleton 2014; Denwood & Piatigorsky 1983]. The Buddha then questions Udāyin about his own school's doctrine of the "highest splendor" or "highest colour" (*paramo vaṇṇo*) [Jayatilleke 1963; SuttaCentral]. Because Udāyin cannot define what this splendor is, the Buddha compares his assertion to a man professing passionate love for the most beautiful woman in the land without ever having seen or known who she is [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995].

Moving beyond Sakuludāyin's vague tenets, the Buddha expounds progressive meditative attainments—including the four absorptions (*jhāna*)—and the true path leading to an entirely pleasant world [Hazra 1994]. In the context of discussing the recollection of past lives, the sutta notably quotes the abstract formula of conditionality / dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) without appending the standard twelve links [Shulman 2014]. Although Sakuludāyin is impressed by the discourse, his followers prevent him from taking ordination and practicing under the Buddha [Dhivan & Sagaraghosa 2011].

The text has a full Chinese Āgama parallel in the *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 208) [SuttaCentral], which DharmaNexus automatically aligns with T 26.57 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-language reuse in Chinese translations such as T 90 (鞞摩肅經) and Sanskrit parallels such as the *Daśabalasūtra* and *Dharmaskandha* [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the sutta exhibits extensive textual overlap with the *Vekhanasa Sutta* (MN 80), which covers a closely parallel dialogue [Rogell 2003; DharmaNexus], as well as the *Mahāsakuludāyi Sutta* (MN 77), the *Poṭṭhapāda Sutta* (DN 9), and formulaic sequences on ascetic training shared with DN 2, DN 10, AN 3, and AN 4 [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
